primary_diagnosis: Thoracoabdominal Radiculopathy / Intercostal Nerve Entrapment Syndrome vs Functional Flank Dyspepsia
clinical_reasoning: Patient reports localized heaviness and discomfort in the abdominal flank rather than epigastric burning, without acute peritoneal signs. Negative intra-abdominal ultrasound findings and lack of gastrointestinal alarm symptoms support the clinician's diagnostic impression of a neuropathic or musculoskeletal etiology (intercostal neuralgia or thoracoabdominal radiculopathy). Neurological assessment and confirmatory imaging are indicated.
recommended_tests: Focused Thoracolumbar Spine & Abdominal Wall Physical Examination (Carnett's test)
Spinal MRI / Nerve Conduction Study (if radicular symptoms persist)
Basic Metabolic Panel and Routine Urinalysis (to exclude renal colic)
